notes: The generic longest-cycle fallback adds a triangular internal connector detour near the back-straight hairpin. The FIA circuit map identifies the direct Grand Prix chain retained in the already registered named source. The exact registered source coordinates and traversal direction are retained without diagram tracing or distance fitting. Travel direction remains provisional. Main public timing stays missing.

source.name: Mapzen Terrain Tiles
attribution: Global elevation data courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey and NOAA.

sources.notes: Road height is sampled from the existing approximately 79 m terrain raster and compressed to a 0.5 m interpolation tolerance relative to those samples; this is not road-surface survey accuracy. Station distances use the midpoint of corresponding border stations, not an official length measurement. There is no saved GPS start gate; the simulation begins at the first trace coordinate. Curbs and bend labels are geometry-based illustrations, not extracted from imagery or verified real curb locations; widths, heights and colours are assumed. Banking is unknown and assumed zero. Source border coordinates retain their separate feature-level licence; invalid cross-sections are interpolated. Imagery is an external display resource subject to provider terms; no image bytes are included.

measurement.note: Sparse paired road-limit image observations on the corrected Grand Prix source. RGB proposals served only as authoring candidates; all selected positions are inspected on the pinned native image. Apron and shared-pavement branch openings use estimated virtual joins; straight-edge observations constrain false shadow and run-off excursions. The two edges interpolate linearly between corresponding observations, preserving source coordinates and driving order. Imagery resolution is not survey accuracy. Curbs remain illustrative, banking unknown and raster elevations estimated. On the back straight (source stations 1224–1584) and the start straight (1764 through closure to 132), intermediate observations are intersections of each source cross-section with two visible edge lines fitted independently from endpoint image observations. Covered bridge/gantry spans follow those fitted lines; their hidden ground edges are not direct pixel observations. These fits do not use a nominal width.

borderInference.note: Road-border estimates reconstructed from complete pairs of sparse image-edge measurements. Each pair defines its own road section; the original trace is preserved and constrains station displacement and route order. Linear intervals, junction openings and curbs remain estimates, not surveyed racing limits. Every saved edge station and anchor requires pinned-image coverage during authoring. No automatic evidence scores are claimed.
